arguments.spec:
# Async pipeline repair — three seeded, INTERACTING defects (project 59, repair_async_pipeline_defects)

`src/` is a small job pipeline: an IO seam (`src/io.mjs`), a shared tally (`src/metrics.mjs`), a downstream record
sink (`src/sink.mjs`) and the pipeline that drives them (`src/pipeline.mjs`), with three seeded defects:

- a floating promise — `runPipeline` starts `sink.write(...)` but never awaits it, so the caller is told a job is
  done while the write is still in flight;
- a lost update — `record` in the shared tally reads the current count, then does an io turn, then writes the
  stale value back, so concurrent increments overwrite each other;
- a swallowed error — `execute`'s catch-all turns a thrown failure into an absent value and `runPipeline` always
  reports status "ok", so a broken job is reported as a success and still reaches the sink.

Repair the code only. Do not rewrite any module, do not change any exported name, and do not weaken the suite.
scenarios/ and test/ are FROZEN evidence, digest-checked on every run — never edit them, never add a dependency
(the sandbox is offline). Nothing in this fixture may sleep, poll or read the clock: every asynchronous step goes
through the injected `io` seam, and ordering is decided by the code under test — a failure here is a defect, never
flake.

The deliverable is repair/manifest.json: `repaired` lists exactly the ids of the frozen scenarios that genuinely
pass right now; every id you list is executed on every run, so listing one that still fails takes the whole build
red with it. `complete: true` requires every scenario this fixture defines to be listed — reserved for the last
card.

The three defects, one per concern:
- floating promise (src/pipeline.mjs, `runPipeline`): `sink.write(...)` is called but not awaited.
- swallowed error (src/pipeline.mjs, `execute` + `runPipeline`): the catch-all discards the thrown error and every
  job is unconditionally reported `status: "ok"`, including ones that threw, and the failed job's placeholder
  value still reaches the sink.
- lost update (src/metrics.mjs, `record`): the current tally is read BEFORE the io turn instead of after, so two
  concurrent calls both read the same stale value and one increment is lost.

How to plan this: one card per defect. The sink scenario (`the-sink-keeps-job-order-and-skips-failures`) and the
failure-reporting scenarios overlap the floating-promise and swallowed-error defects — one scenario
(`the-sink-keeps-job-order-and-skips-failures`) needs both fixed before it goes green — so those two cards are
sequenced (dependsOn), not run in parallel. The lost-update card is independent in source (src/metrics.mjs) but
every card writes the same repair/manifest.json, so it is chained too. Reserve the last card for the completeness
pass.

Acceptance: `npm test`, offline, with the fixture's own toolchain. Never add a dependency.

# Plan: repair-async-pipeline-defects (project 59)

Verified empirically before writing this graph: copied src/, scenarios/, test/ into a scratch dir and ran the six
frozen `scenarios[].check()` functions directly at each hypothetical fix stage.

- Baseline (no fixes): all 6 scenarios FAIL.
- +floating-promise fix only (`await sink.write(...)` in `runPipeline`): `the-sink-is-complete-when-the-pipeline-resolves`
  flips PASS. `the-sink-keeps-job-order-and-skips-failures` still FAILS, now on the job-order/skip-failures
  assertion instead of the in-flight assertion — confirming it needs the swallowed-error fix too.
- +swallowed-error fix on top (`execute` returns `{status, value|error}`, `runPipeline` spreads that outcome and
  only writes to the sink when `status === "ok"`): `the-sink-keeps-job-order-and-skips-failures`,
  `a-failing-job-is-reported-as-failed`, `a-failure-does-not-hide-the-other-results` all flip PASS. The two
  lost-update scenarios are still failing, untouched by this fix, confirming independence from pipeline.mjs.
- +lost-update fix on top (`record` reads the current count AFTER `await io.yield()`, not before): the remaining
  two scenarios (`concurrent-records-of-one-key-do-not-lose-updates`, `interleaved-records-across-keys-stay-exact`)
  flip PASS. All 6 green. Full `npm test` with all 6 ids listed and `complete: true` passes 5/5.

Four cards, linear dependsOn chain (every card writes repair/manifest.json, so isolation requires the chain
regardless of which cards share a src file):
1. `fix-pipeline-floating-promise-defect` — src/pipeline.mjs, awaits the sink write.
2. `fix-pipeline-swallowed-error-defect` (depends on 1) — src/pipeline.mjs, execute()/runPipeline() report real
   status and skip the sink on failure.
3. `fix-metrics-lost-update-defect` (depends on 2) — src/metrics.mjs, reorders the read to after the io yield.
4. `repair-completeness-verify-and-close` (depends on 3) — manifest-only, confirms all 6 ids and flips
   `complete: true`.

All four cards: testability not_testable (frozen verifier is the acceptance, test/ and scenarios/ are digest-frozen
and outside write scope), acceptanceCommand npm test, complexity 25 (fix cards) / 20 (completeness) — all at or
under the 40 ceiling so replay never blocks on candidate-fit.
